item.content:encoded:
OpenAI scientist proposes shared limits on frontier AI development

Category: AI

OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has proposed that frontier AI developers agree on shared capability limits based on perplexity and other measures, and refrain from crossing them until their ability to monitor and understand model behavior meets defined safety milestones. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman endorsed the proposal, but Pachocki specified no initial threshold, start date or enforcement mechanism. It remains a call for an industry agreement, not an adopted restriction [21][33][2][25]. Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token, with lower scores indicating better predictions. Pachocki says the metric can track pretraining progress as task-based tests become outdated. He argues that AI could accelerate research into pretraining methods as early as 2027, potentially outpacing improvements in safety monitoring [33][21]. He also acknowledged that perplexity alone cannot provide a common yardstick: labs use different training mixtures and evaluation data, and the measure misses some capability gains from reasoning after pretraining. Pachocki’s proposal calls for shared evaluation, red-team and transparency standards alongside staged limits, with further development dependent on concrete advances in monitoring [3][18][19].

I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone

— Jakub Pachocki, OpenAI chief scientist (The Hindu BusinessLine)

Key Points

  • Published scores: OpenAI reported log-perplexity of about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 and 0.91 for GPT-4; Pachocki linked scores below 0.8 to emerging mathematics and cybersecurity capabilities, and cited results on open math problems at about 0.76 [33][3][19].
  • What drove the curve: OpenAI attributed most of the steep decline in its 2026 loss curve to long-term research and compute investment, with AI automation contributing a smaller share [19][18].
  • Uncertain next threshold: Pachocki forecast further transformative capabilities as log-perplexity reaches 0.68–0.70, but said their nature is unknown and current evaluations may not test for them [3][19].
  • Policy debate: The Straits Times reported that Democrats’ midterm gains could renew congressional scrutiny and efforts to introduce AI safety rules, while President Donald Trump opposes broad restrictions on AI development [7].

Perspectives

Jakub Pachocki, OpenAI chief scientist: Pachocki said publishing OpenAI’s internal measurements gives competitors a clearer view of the company’s position, but he judged shared safety measures more urgent than that competitive cost [33][3].

Sources: OpenAI

Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft AI chief executive: Suleyman publicly called Pachocki’s proposal “super important” and praised OpenAI for making the case for transparency [26].

Sources: Dealroom

Alexandr Wang, Meta AI executive: Wang warned that technological progress could outpace people’s ability to understand or control its consequences and called for urgent advances in safety, alignment and security [29].

Sources: TradingView

Timeline

  • July 2026: Employees at OpenAI, Anthropic and other firms called for limits on the pace of frontier AI development [2].
  • September 2026: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a call to slow development [2].
  • 10 November 2026: OpenAI released a study on model monitorability and reasoning behavior [1][18].
  • 22 November 2026: Pachocki published OpenAI’s proposal and internal perplexity measurements [33][21].

Technical Details

  • OpenAI reported log-perplexity, or cross-entropy loss, measured on a held-out evaluation set drawn from its internal codebase [33][18].
  • OpenAI’s Nov. 10 study found that AI models can solve problems or control the contents of their inference records without writing out their reasoning, making it harder to monitor them through those records [1][18].

AI sell-off exposes risks in data-center financing

Category: AI

The AI-stock sell-off has intensified scrutiny of the debt and corporate guarantees financing data-center expansion. Nvidia’s guarantees totaled $118 billion as of Oct. 25, while its commitments to smaller cloud providers were estimated at $32 billion over the next several years. On a Nov. 17 earnings call, interim chief executive Colette Kress said Nvidia would scrutinize AI cloud companies’ financial strength and prioritize sites with visible, durable demand [16]. Those commitments have helped reassure lenders financing data centers and computing clusters. But analysts warn that banks may now be less willing to extend bridge loans to smaller providers whose debt they expect to resell. Nvidia’s tighter scrutiny could affect companies that lack established revenue or strong backers [16][57]. Jon von Tetzchner, CEO and co-founder of San Francisco-based Vivaldi, questioned whether many AI applications are useful. An unnamed worker at a major San Francisco AI company told the BBC he expected a downturn and feared it would affect him [14][12].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

On GPU-backed loans to unrated borrowers, credit committees will become much more selective because no bank wants to get stuck holding unsellable bridge loans on its own balance sheet.

— Henning Stein, finance fellow at Cambridge Judge Business School (The Banker)

Key Points

  • Policy watch: Investors were awaiting U.S. October personal consumption expenditures inflation data, scheduled for Wednesday during a shortened holiday week [80].
  • IPO signal: Anthropic’s record $107 billion initial public offering raised much more than expected but failed to lift shares of backers Google and Amazon or offering partners Broadcom, AMD and Nvidia [11].
  • City spillover: San Francisco’s AI boom has brought business to services such as Paw Perk, a dog-walking service for startup offices. Rents and house prices have risen, while office vacancies have fallen [12].
  • Additional financing: Nvidia, Google and Microsoft participated in a concurrent $26 billion private placement, bringing combined gross proceeds from the IPO and placement to more than $107 billion [92].
  • AI labels: Vivaldi co-founder Jon von Tetzchner likened companies’ rush to adopt AI labels to the earlier blockchain and crypto boom. He said some use popular technology labels to attract investors despite a questionable connection to their existing businesses [14].
  • Long contracts: The disclosed commitments include multiyear purchases and equipment leases extending as far as 2045; $186.2 billion in fixed commitments include termination rights or conditions [93].
  • Market losses: Taiwan’s Taiex lost more than $500 billion in market value over the week, while South Korea’s Kospi shed more than $1.8 trillion from its June peak, according to Financial Times estimates [22].
  • AI spending: Gartner projected global AI-related investment of $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027 [52].
  • Investor flows: Goldman Sachs data showed hedge funds had sold global equities for a third consecutive week, with short sales exceeding long purchases by 1.5 to 1 [61].
  • Regional demand: Santa Lucia Asset Management CEO Florian Weidinger warned that China’s shift toward domestic AI hardware could restrict Nvidia’s access to Asia, while competition from more chipmakers and weaker demand could squeeze margins and prompt order revisions [58].
  • Enterprise demand: Anthropic had 11,900 customers, with more than 100 generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue, according to figures reported around the listing [92].
  • China’s buying measures: Chinese exchanges also announced transaction-fee cuts, and Shenzhen proposed a market-making mechanism for its ChiNext board [15].
  • Investor rationale: Notable Capital said its research found developers chose Claude over ChatGPT 70% of the time, reversing the prior year’s pattern [111].

Perspectives

Malik Ahmed Khan, Morningstar stock analyst: Khan said Anthropic’s ability to complete a large capital raise in a difficult market could encourage OpenAI to pursue a public listing [11].

Sources: San Francisco Examiner

Anthropic: Chief Executive Dario Amodei said the company expects to use debt financing at some point [131].

Sources: Le Parisien

GIC: The Singapore sovereign wealth fund said Claude Code’s popularity among developers and model improvements driving enterprise adoption informed its investments in Anthropic [111].

Sources: TechCrunch

South Korean finance ministry and financial regulators: Officials said long-term AI growth expectations remain intact and warned against excessive anxiety or panic selling [22].

Sources: Financial Times

Dillin Wu, Pepperstone strategist: Wu said the support measures may steady prices temporarily but are unlikely to reverse the reassessment of AI-related valuations or draw foreign investors back [3].

Sources: Yonhap News Agency

JPMorgan analysts: The bank’s analysts described the pullback as mostly AI-related deleveraging and said they still viewed the AI growth cycle as durable, citing lower leverage and improved positioning [80].

Sources: The Economic Times

Timeline

  • 2025: DeepSeek released a low-cost model rivaling leading US systems [50]
  • 17 November 2026: Nvidia said it would vet AI cloud providers’ finances more closely [16]
  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic began trading after a record-setting public offering [11]
  • 20 November 2026: Anthropic shares fell during their first full trading session [11]
  • 2024: GIC researched Anthropic before making its first investment [111]
  • March 2025: Anthropic closed its Series E funding round at a $61.5 billion valuation [102]
  • September 2025: GIC first invested in Anthropic’s Series F round [111]
  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT [111]
  • 20 November 2026: Nvidia fell 14% as U.S. technology stocks sold off [79].
  • 22 November 2026: South Korea announced plans to prepare its stabilization fund [15].
  • 23 November 2026: The Kospi fell as much as 5.8% before paring losses, while Taiwan’s Taiex rebounded 2.5% [52].
  • 24 November 2026: South Korea’s temporary share-buyback rule easing is due to begin [3].
  • 30 November 2026: China’s lower minimum margin ratio is scheduled to take effect [15].

Technical Details

  • Nvidia guarantees: Nvidia’s guarantees totaled $118 billion as of Oct. 25, while its commitments to smaller cloud providers were estimated at $32 billion over the next several years. Those arrangements helped reassure lenders that borrowers could obtain GPUs and generate data-center revenue [16].
  • GPU-backed bridge loans: Banks have financed data centers and computing clusters with bridge loans backed by graphics processing units, expecting to syndicate the debt to institutional investors. Lenders may now require stronger evidence of contracted revenue and project completion [16].
  • South Korea’s stabilization fund: Financial firms and other institutions created the 10.76 trillion-won fund, valued at nearly $8 billion, to support markets during sharp downturns. The government said it was preparing the fund for immediate activation [15].
  • China margin financing: The exchanges’ reduction of the minimum margin ratio from 100% to 80% means an investor putting up 1 million yuan could theoretically borrow enough to buy 1.25 million yuan in shares, increasing both leverage and buying capacity [3].

Industry Impact

  • Semiconductors: South Korea’s Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are major memory-chip suppliers for AI applications, leaving the Kospi particularly sensitive to changes in expectations for AI demand [27][78].
  • Power equipment supply chain: AI data-center demand is drawing on turbine suppliers that also serve aviation and energy infrastructure. Reported disruptions include delays to container ships and a planned supersonic airliner, as well as construction problems at power stations on two continents [4].
  • Adjacent infrastructure: Selling also hit optical-products maker Corning and power provider Bloom Energy, which supply data-centre connectivity and electricity [79].
  • Venture capital: GIC, Baillie Gifford and Notable Capital invested more than $4.5 billion across Anthropic’s later funding rounds, and GIC held about 1% of the company after the IPO, according to a person familiar with its finances [102][111].
  • AI infrastructure financing: An investment-grade credit rating could give Anthropic access to the $8.6 trillion U.S. investment-grade corporate bond market; suppliers including Broadcom and Nvidia have guaranteed loans to AI compute providers [43].

Historical Background

South Korea’s securities-market stabilization fund was established in 2020 during the Covid-19 pandemic, according to CNBC [15]. Local media cited by Yonhap said it was last used during the 2008 global financial crisis [3]. China had raised its minimum margin ratio for credit-financed stock purchases from 80% to 100% in January 2026; the exchanges’ new reduction reverses that increase after 10 months [85].

Business Angle

  • One investor cited Samsung and SK Hynix trading at three to four times forward earnings, compared with Anthropic at 20 times projected revenue, as a reason to distinguish chip suppliers from AI developers [57].
  • UBS’s Eva Lee said investors seeking value in the AI sell-off could look for companies with strong balance sheets, sound fundamentals and the capacity to buy back shares [2].
  • Portfolio manager Owen Lamont argued that companies may sell shares either because they are overvalued or to fund AI investment, so equity issuance alone does not rule out an investment opportunity [22].

Q&A

Q: What indicators could show whether Taiwan’s sell-off is easing?

Anthropic mathematician says Claude outpaced him near proof's finish

Category: AI

Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says the company’s Claude AI took a larger role as they worked on a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a famous problem about prime numbers. Alpöge said he guided the effort by combining two mathematical ideas, but Claude moved faster than he did near the end. Separate Lean and Mathlib groups have since verified the formalized proof [1][17]. The collaboration lasted about six weeks, from early October to Nov. 16, according to Alpöge’s account [6]. He has not yet published a readable mathematical explanation, leaving researchers to work out the argument behind the computer-checked result [29][8]. The announcement came a day after Anthropic’s stock-market debut, prompting questions about its timing. Alpöge called the timing “horrible” and said he would have finished earlier if he could. He denied that the release was coordinated with the listing [17][29].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

It’s a monumental moment in human history. It’s really the biggest thing I think that’s ever happened in mathematics

— Brian Conrey, leading Riemann specialist (Taipei Times)

Did you know: Before the Riemann claim, Alpöge had used Claude while posting a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture, another longstanding mathematics problem [3].

Key Points

  • A specific advance: While extending Stepanov’s method, Claude proposed setting the theta-lift chain length to √X, which Alpöge said helped move the work forward [1].
  • Scope: Alpöge said the proof also covers the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions [8].
  • Company process: Alpöge said he consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before publishing [10].

Perspectives

Nestor Guillen, New York University mathematics professor: Guillen said Alpöge’s work was a more human-directed collaboration than OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes announcement, with AI working “more like a tool” rather than appearing as an autonomous authority [10].

Sources: Taipei Times

Shing-Tung Yau, Fields Medal-winning mathematician: Yau said machines still lag people in posing problems even as their problem-solving ability grows, and suggested mathematical research could increasingly find results first and examine them afterward [29].

Sources: South China Morning Post

Timeline

  • October 2026: Alpöge began working with Claude on the proof, according to his account [6]
  • 16 November 2026: Alpöge said the six-week effort ended four days before publication [6]
  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share [6]
  • 20 November 2026: Alpöge announced his Claude-assisted proof claim online [17][29]

Industry Impact

  • AI research: OpenAI had recently publicized hundreds of human-supervised mathematical proofs, according to Semafor [12].

Historical Background

Anthropic said in August that Claude had improved a bound related to the Riemann hypothesis but had not proved it [10]. In September, rival OpenAI said its AI helped solve part of the Navier–Stokes problem, another Millennium Prize challenge. That claim had not received formal recognition, according to the reporting [32][18].

Q&A

Q: What would need to happen before Alpöge could receive the Clay prize?

A: The solution must appear in a qualifying publication, then undergo at least two years of scrutiny and gain general acceptance in the mathematics community [8].

Study finds coding-agent instruction files grow 226% over time

Category: AI

A new study of AI coding-agent instructions found that files such as CLAUDE.md grew by 226% over their lifetimes as additions outpaced deletions across 1,867 repositories. Researcher Kushal Chakrabarti analyzed 247,694 instruction lifetimes and attributed the pattern to agents’ imperfect recall of why older instructions were added [6]. The paper, revised Nov. 20, reports that comments recording the reasoning behind instructions cut excess prompt size by 99.3% in constructed tests. In small-scale tests in real repositories, the approach also improved instruction-following by 17.7% [6]. The coding agent Claude Code is also being used for projects beyond conventional software development, including hobbyist-built apps and hardware prototypes [2][7]. A separate review of the free coding agent Freebuff warns that it logs mouse and keyboard input and may use submitted information for advertising and AI training [5].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

If English is the new code, why don't we have comments yet?

— Kushal Chakrabarti (arXiv)

Key Points

  • Prompt drift: The paper measured a net increase of 4.7 instructions per commit and found that the chance of deleting an instruction falls geometrically as it ages [6].
  • Tuning workflow: Sybil Solutions’ open-source skill benchmarks local-model serving using interleaved control runs, a memory cap and long-context checks. ExplainX says it did not independently rerun the published performance figures [3].
  • Prototype hardware: One Claude Code project used an ESP32-C3, motion sensor and OLED display in an hourglass prototype that controls iPhone app access. Its planned 211-LED circuit board still needs to be manufactured and tested [7].
  • Paid access: Claude Code is not included in Anthropic’s free subscription, and Tom’s Guide lists Claude Pro at $20 a month as the starting paid plan [2].

Perspectives

Notebookcheck reviewer: The review argues that Freebuff collects more data than is common among ChatGPT-like services, citing interest profiles derived from user input and the collection of device information [5].

Sources: Notebookcheck

Technical Details

  • Deletion-cost model: The paper says that once the reasoning behind an instruction is lost, deciding whether it can safely be removed can require O(2^|D|) work in a prompt containing |D| instructions [6].
  • Comparison with context maintainers: The paper reports that comment-based prompts were smaller than those produced by existing context-maintenance approaches in real-world and coding-convention settings [6].

Scientific Significance

  • Failure risk: The paper warns that instruction accumulation may continue until agents become nonfunctional; it says growth otherwise stops only when project history ends or someone rewrites the file wholesale [6].

Q&A

Q: How stable is Freebuff’s free access?

A: The review says available models and free-use limits can change and vary by country. It reports that DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast was limited to three hours and that larger models were increasingly tied to paid plans [5].

item.content:encoded:
Microsoft warns AI-driven patching could fuel months of further outages

Category: Technology

Microsoft President Brad Smith warned Sunday that technology outages could continue for months as companies and governments race to patch vulnerabilities and upgrade aging systems. His warning follows separate failures affecting U.S. aviation, Microsoft services, banks, Apple and the National Security Agency; intelligence officials say they have found no evidence the incidents were coordinated cyberattacks [6][23][3][1]. Smith said artificial intelligence is making it easier for defenders to find software flaws, but those discoveries can also help attackers, while rushed fixes leave less time for testing. Older infrastructure adds to the risk: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said some critical systems, including internet-connected firmware and industrial equipment, cannot readily be patched [23][9]. Smith said Microsoft’s own outage was not caused by AI or a cyberattack, but by an interaction between an earlier software update and a newer one that changed network traffic. The company has published two incident reports, completed nine corrective measures and identified 13 more, he said [27][23].

Primary Source: View original article

The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now.

— Brad Smith, Microsoft president (The Verge)

Key Points

  • IT strain: A cybersecurity professional told the Guardian that the relentless exposure of software flaws had left their team “exhausted” [1].
  • Exploit pressure: The FBI warned Nov. 13 that hackers were using the open-source AI tool ARTEX, with some intrusions reaching administrator access in under three hours [2].
  • Flight impact: The Federal Aviation Administration’s ground stop led to more than 18,000 canceled flights [1].
  • Patch volume: Microsoft fixed 1,413 vulnerabilities in October, exceeding its previous full-year record, according to Oren Etzioni’s analysis [2].
  • System design: IGEL Chief Technology Officer John Walsh said critical infrastructure should be built to keep essential services running when a component is compromised or unavailable [23].

Perspectives

Microsoft: Brad Smith called for closer cooperation between technology companies and governments to share information about emerging cyber threats [27].

Sources: National Herald

Oren Etzioni: Etzioni expects Windows, iOS and Chrome to become more secure than ever within a year or two as AI helps find and fix a finite supply of bugs [2].

Sources: GeekWire

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent: Bessent said Americans should not worry about the stability of financial institutions, describing banks as among the most resilient U.S. companies after decades of cybersecurity investment [23].

Sources: Newsweek

Industry Impact

  • Business continuity: CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said some companies are taking services offline rather than risking a breach, describing the choice as “breach or break” [7].
  • Exploit speed: Kurtz said AI agents can compare a patch with unpatched code and automate an exploit within an hour, a task that might once have taken a nation-state actor weeks [7].

Historical Background

A contract to modernize the Federal Aviation Administration’s communications network was awarded in 2002 to a company now known as L3Harris. The work has involved replacing copper communication lines with fiber-optic cable. A newly installed router at an Arkansas site malfunctioned during that ongoing project [1].

Q&A

Q: Does every newly reported software flaw get exploited?

A: No. VulnCheck counted 100,222 published vulnerabilities in 2026 as of Nov. 13, but about 1.4% had appeared on its list of flaws known to be exploited [20].

Action Items

  • Install available security updates on personal devices: Microsoft President Brad Smith advised consumers to apply patches sent to phones and laptops promptly [23].

item.content:encoded:
Rockstar Games’ GTA VI sets $3.79 billion first-day sales record

Category: Technology

Grand Theft Auto VI generated an estimated $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, Nov. 19, while Rockstar Games said 32.5 million copies had sold before launch. The company called it the biggest entertainment launch in history; the previous entry in the series, Grand Theft Auto V, took three days to reach $1 billion in sales after its 2013 release [10][27]. The new game puts players in the roles of Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a criminal couple in the fictional, Florida-inspired state of Leonida. Lucia is the franchise’s first non-optional female lead, and their relationship is central to the story alongside the series’ open-world crime and satire [17][18]. The game launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles; Rockstar has not announced a date for its online mode [31][26]. GTA VI received eight nominations for The Game Awards, including game of the year. The ceremony is scheduled for Dec. 10 [18].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you.

— Sam Houser, president and founder of Rockstar Games (KSL.com)

Key Points

  • Console performance: GTA VI is capped at 30 frames per second on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5 Pro, with no 60-fps performance mode, according to the report [32].
  • Score split: Metacritic showed a critic score of 99 based on more than 150 reviews, while its player score fell to 5.6 by Nov. 22 as GTA and Zelda fans targeted each other’s games with negative reviews [6].
  • Digital copies: The reported retail editions contain activation codes rather than game discs, leaving buyers without a disc to lend or resell [11].
  • Easter eggs: Players’ early discoveries in Leonida included a recreation of Dexter Morgan’s Florida apartment and kill-room setup [1].
  • Livestream audience: Viewers watched more than 132 million hours of GTA VI streams on Twitch, YouTube and Kick on launch day, with concurrent audiences nearing 8 million [26].

Perspectives

Rockstar Games design team: Vice president of design Stephen Donkin said the team built missions to blur the boundary between on-mission and off-mission play, letting dialogue connect open-world activity with the protagonists’ story [8].

Sources: TechRadar

Adrienne Shaw, Temple University media studies professor: Shaw said Rockstar’s choices around representation also reflect a business effort to reach a diverse player base, rather than simply an act of goodwill [17].

Sources: NPR

Tim Burchett, U.S. representative from Tennessee: Burchett criticized the game as a “crime manual” and argued that its violence could make children less sensitive to real-world violence [32].

Sources: Storm Media

South Florida officials: Some officials questioned spending public resources on a $3.9 million promotional agreement tied to a game known for car theft and gunplay [18].

Sources: LAist

Timeline

  • 25 June 2026: GTA VI preorders opened ahead of its November release [31]
  • 19 November 2026: GTA VI launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles [31][18]
  • 22 November 2026: Metacritic user score stood at 5.6 during rival fan review attacks [6]
  • 10 December 2026: The Game Awards ceremony is scheduled, with GTA VI nominated eight times [18]

Industry Impact

  • Telecommunications: Chorus New Zealand forecast about 35 petabytes of extra network traffic around the game’s release as customers downloaded its 212-gigabyte file [18].
  • Food delivery: DoorDash recorded a surge in late-night energy-drink orders around launch, while Uber Eats offered food promotions designed for players [26].
  • Local promotion: Miami-Dade County agreed to a $3.9 million promotional deal with Rockstar, including a “Welcome to Vice City” display at the Miami Heat arena [18].

Historical Background

Grand Theft Auto began in 1997, and the series’ third installment moved it into a three-dimensional open world in 2001 [11][15]. Grand Theft Auto V, released in 2013, has sold more than 230 million copies [10][18].

item.content:encoded:
Signal blocks mobile AI agents from capturing private chats

Category: Technology

Signal has added protections to block operating-system AI assistants from reading chats on iOS 27 and Android, saying screen access could expose conversations outside its encrypted messaging service [1][4][12]. On iOS, the app blocks screenshots and recordings by default, hides chats from the App Switcher and prevents Siri AI from viewing its screen. On Android, it enables Screen Security when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen [2][6]. Signal says messages can be captured after the app decrypts them for display and then made available to an AI system’s local database or remote server, beyond Signal’s control [6][7]. Users can turn off the protection, but Signal warns that doing so could expose their own messages and those of their contacts. The app cannot offer the same protection on macOS; Signal advises Mac users to exclude it from Siri in system settings [2][1]. Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for clearer technical documentation and a way for developers to opt apps out of AI access [8][7].

We will now be taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where we can detect an AI assistant attempting to read your Signal screen

— Meredith Whittaker, Signal president (BleepingComputer)

Key Points

  • Earlier protection: Signal introduced a safeguard in May 2025 to block Microsoft’s Recall screen-capture feature from capturing chats in its Windows 11 app [1][5][9].
  • Temporary override: On iOS, users can temporarily disable screenshot blocking; Signal restores it automatically after 10 minutes [2].
  • Other access routes: Signal says screenshot controls cannot prevent agents from reading app data through device files, while third-party agents such as Meta Muse may use Android Accessibility permissions [3][8].
  • Messages at risk: Signal’s concern extends to disappearing messages: a separate screen-capture system such as Microsoft Recall could use optical character recognition to read them and store searchable records [7][10].

Action Items

  • Check Signal’s screen-protection settings: Update Signal and check that “Block Siri AI” is enabled under Settings > App Security on iOS; Mac users can add Signal to the Siri Excluded Apps list in System Settings [1][2].

item.title: UN climate summit ends without pact as fossil fuel dispute stalls talks
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Canada, World, Science / Climate Diplomacy)
item.description: The COP31 United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Nov. 22 without an overarching agreement after nearly 200 countries failed to resolve disputes over fossil fuels and climate finance. The talks ran about two days past their scheduled close, making COP31 the longest COP conference on record. The final draft omitted an explicit reference to fossil fuels, prompting the European Union, the United Kingdom, Panama and vulnerable island states to reject it [24][9][18]. The draft referred indirectly to the 2023 COP28 commitment to transition away from fossil fuels but did not spell out a pathway or reaffirm the wording. Oil-producing countries, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, resisted explicit references to fossil fuels, while poorer countries objected that the proposal did not set concrete funding levels for adaptation. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen said fossil fuels and finance were the main obstacles; summit president Murat Kurum said he would not put forward a replacement draft [3][54][16]. Countries agreed on separate measures, including a program to support workers and communities through the energy transition and a plan to assess adaptation progress. More than 80 countries backed Türkiye’s proposed goal of raising electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, but the goal was not part of an adopted overarching pact. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he would seek advice on possible reforms to the consensus-based negotiating process. The next summit is scheduled for Addis Ababa [61][3][24][20].

UN climate summit ends without pact as fossil fuel dispute stalls talks

Category: World

The COP31 United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Nov. 22 without an overarching agreement after nearly 200 countries failed to resolve disputes over fossil fuels and climate finance. The talks ran about two days past their scheduled close, making COP31 the longest COP conference on record. The final draft omitted an explicit reference to fossil fuels, prompting the European Union, the United Kingdom, Panama and vulnerable island states to reject it [24][9][18]. The draft referred indirectly to the 2023 COP28 commitment to transition away from fossil fuels but did not spell out a pathway or reaffirm the wording. Oil-producing countries, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, resisted explicit references to fossil fuels, while poorer countries objected that the proposal did not set concrete funding levels for adaptation. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen said fossil fuels and finance were the main obstacles; summit president Murat Kurum said he would not put forward a replacement draft [3][54][16]. Countries agreed on separate measures, including a program to support workers and communities through the energy transition and a plan to assess adaptation progress. More than 80 countries backed Türkiye’s proposed goal of raising electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, but the goal was not part of an adopted overarching pact. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he would seek advice on possible reforms to the consensus-based negotiating process. The next summit is scheduled for Addis Ababa [61][3][24][20].

Temperatures keep shattering records. Climate extremes keep intensifying. Emissions remain far too high. And every delay makes our task harder and more costly.

— António Guterres, United Nations secretary-general (PBS NewsHour (Associated Press))

Did you know: The first draft of the proposed pact mentioned fossil fuels six times, while later drafts removed direct references [3][13].

Key Points

  • Emissions record: A 440 Megatonnes analysis found Canada had cut emissions 8.5% from 2005 levels by 2023, compared with an average 32% reduction across the other G7 countries [30][83].
  • Electricity target: The proposed 35% electricity share by 2035 compares with about 23% today. Coal supplies roughly one-third of global electricity and fossil gas about one-fifth, so the emissions effect would depend on how the power is generated [95][47].
  • Australian fallout: Australian opposition leader Angus Taylor called for Climate Minister Chris Bowen to resign, while Prime Minister Anthony Albanese did not say whether he would dismiss him [36].
  • Finance gap: The draft dropped a proposed annual adaptation-finance figure of $120 billion, while estimated adaptation needs in the Global South alone totaled about $500 billion a year [58][20].
  • Emissions gap: The UN Environment Programme’s modeled pathway requires greenhouse-gas emissions to fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 from 2025 levels. Full implementation of current national pledges would cut emissions far less, putting the world on an estimated 2.6°C warming trajectory [48].
  • Legal challenge: Climate advocates have asked the Federal Court to require Ottawa to bring its 2030 emissions plan into compliance with the Net-Zero Accountability Act, which sets no fines or penalties for missed targets [30][84].
  • Carbon removal: The draft's explicit reference to carbon dioxide removal would have been a first in a COP final agreement. Natural approaches such as tree planting face limits of scale and permanence, while technological options remain controversial and not well advanced [27].
  • Science dispute: The final days also saw disagreement over the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s work, with UK climate negotiator Kate Hughes saying the draft moved backward on science [100].
  • US absence: The United States sent no delegation for the second consecutive year after President Donald Trump’s administration withdrew from the Paris climate agreement [10][25].
  • COP initiatives: At the Turkey talks, Canada announced up to $10 million for climate-risk and early-warning systems; nearly 100 countries separately backed a proposal to raise electricity’s share of final energy use to 35% by 2035 [82].

Perspectives

European Union: Speaking for the bloc, Irish Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said it would not endorse a climate decision that failed to mention fossil fuels, arguing that the omission did not reflect the science or the action required [14].

Sources: PBS NewsHour (Associated Press)

Saudi Arabia and Russia: Saudi Arabia’s delegate Mohammad Ayoub said Arab countries had negotiated in good faith and accounted for only a small share of historical emissions, while Russia warned that moving away from fossil fuels too quickly could cause fuel poverty [3].

Sources: Mercopress

Like-Minded Developing Countries: India’s representative Amandeep Garg said the draft inadequately reflected equity, historical responsibility and developed countries’ climate-finance obligations, especially in its proposed global targets [37].

Sources: Firstpost

Türkiye COP31 presidency: President Murat Kurum said the presidency had not imposed the text and accepted that countries lacked consensus; Türkiye’s presidency also denied giving any country preferential treatment during the talks [14][35].

Sources: PBS NewsHour (Associated Press)

Climate-process reform advocates: Nikki Reisch of the Center for International Environmental Law argued that requiring every country to agree on every detail is not fit for a climate emergency; former Vice President Al Gore called for a process reflecting majority positions [22].

Sources: Dawn

Sources: The Globe and Mail

Sources: The Globe and Mail

Sources: The Globe and Mail

European Union: The bloc said it could not support a text that failed to address the implementation gap [50].

Sources: Down To Earth

Global Climate and Health Alliance: Executive Director Jeni Miller said the outcome failed to provide a clear fossil-fuel transition plan or financing for countries to prepare their health systems for climate shocks [1].

Sources: Global Issues

Timeline

  • 9 November 2026: COP31 opened in Antalya, with negotiations led jointly by Türkiye and Australia [20].
  • 20 November 2026: The summit’s scheduled closing day passed without agreement on the political text [24][20].
  • 22 November 2026: Delegates ended the record-length summit without adopting the proposed overarching pact [18][9].
  • 2027: COP32 is scheduled to take place in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia [20].
  • 2015: Paris Agreement set the goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C [88]
  • 2023: COP28 agreement called for transition away from fossil fuels [75]
  • 22 November 2026: COP31 ended without consensus on its overarching climate text [50]
  • November 2027: COP32 is scheduled to take place in Ethiopia [3]

Technical Details

  • Carbon capture scale: The draft called for scaling up carbon capture, utilisation and storage to gigatonne levels by 2035, but did not specify how much this would reduce net emissions [50].

Scientific Significance

  • Emissions pathway: In the UNEP scenario summarized in the reporting, warming peaks at about 1.7°C to 1.8°C near mid-century, with roughly a 50% chance of returning to or below 1.5°C by 2100. This is a modeled pathway, not a prediction that those outcomes will occur [48].

Historical Background

The 2015 Paris Agreement established a goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C above preindustrial levels [8][62]. COP31 was the first summit since the 2009 Copenhagen conference to end without an adopted overarching political agreement [24][54].

International Reactions

  • Russia and Saudi Arabia: Both countries sought to keep fossil fuels out of the COP31 agreement [82].
  • 🇬🇧 United Kingdom: UK Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh called the failure to reach a deal immensely disappointing, while saying Britain would continue working with international partners [45].
  • 🇦🇺 Australia: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attributed the breakdown to difficult geopolitical circumstances [3].
  • 🇺🇳 United Nations: Secretary-General António Guterres said he was deeply disappointed that COP31 ended without consensus on an overarching outcome [82].
  • 🇪🇺 European Union: The 27-nation bloc said it could not accept the final proposal, which did not mention fossil fuels [82].

Q&A

Q: Did the collapse cancel commitments made at earlier climate summits?

A: No. The failure to adopt an overarching agreement did not erase existing commitments under prior COP decisions or the Paris Agreement [44][64].

Q: Where will countries resume climate negotiations?

A: Countries are expected to discuss unresolved issues at interim meetings in Bonn before COP32, scheduled for Addis Ababa [20].

Q: Did the failed summit cancel climate commitments countries had already made?

A: No. The failure to adopt a new political declaration did not erase obligations or technical and legal frameworks agreed at previous UN climate conferences [38].

Suspected Ukrainian drones sink Russian corvette, hit second ship off Libya

Category: World

Libya’s eastern administration said a suspected drone attack caused an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at Benghazi on Sunday. Satellite imagery identified the vessel as the Russian navy corvette Merkury and showed it capsized, with only its bow above water [12][15][3]. Two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press that Ukrainian sea drones launched from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya struck the ship. They said four drones were intercepted and two hit. Ukraine has not claimed responsibility, and Russia has not commented [10][8]. Medical sources said 10 people, including Russians and Libyans, suffered minor injuries. Later Sunday, a drone boat hit a second vessel off Benghazi, reportedly a Malta-flagged commercial ship. Libyan naval forces rescued its crew. Military sources said Libyan forces intercepted more than 20 drone boats off the coast [12][6]. The eastern administration said it would investigate jointly with Russia. Its prime minister, Osama Hamad, said the government had formally asked the U.N. General Assembly and Security Council for an international inquiry, including into suspicions that the drones came from western Libya. The U.N. mission in Libya called for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation [12][11].

— United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) (BBC News)

Key Points

  • U.N. request: Hamad also asked the U.N. to verify whether Ukrainian experts are in Libya and called on Kyiv to explain their activities [12].
  • Russian operations: Russia has used Benghazi as a logistical hub for its military operations in Africa and its Mediterranean presence, according to The Hill [20].
  • Distance from front: Benghazi is more than 1,000 miles from southern Ukraine [14][9].
  • Diplomat’s statement: Ukraine’s top diplomat in Washington wrote that the vessels would “no longer be serving the Russian war machine,” without explicitly claiming responsibility [6].

Perspectives

Eastern Libyan administration: It described the suspected strike as a violation of Libyan sovereignty and maritime safety and said it reserved the right to take legal and diplomatic action against anyone found responsible [12].

Jalel Harchaoui, Libya specialist at the Royal United Services Institute: He said Ukraine was likely responsible, while stressing that his view was an informed judgment rather than an official attribution [15].

  • 2011: Uprising toppled Muammar Gaddafi, leaving rival administrations in Libya [15].
  • February 2022: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine [12].

item.content:encoded:
Democrats secure 258 House seats, setting up divided government

Category: World

Democrats have secured at least 258 of 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives, their largest majority since 1992, after North Carolina Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Virginia Foxx in a recount. Republicans hold at least 173 seats, with four contests unresolved. Democrats also won a 56-seat Senate majority, giving them control of both chambers under Republican President Donald Trump beginning in January [15][5][3]. Democrats say their first 100 days will focus on the cost of living and health care, including votes to reverse Republican Medicaid cuts and restore expired Affordable Care Act tax credits. They also plan investigations into the administration and the finances of Trump and his family. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, expected to become speaker, has not ruled out another impeachment effort [1][14]. Trump can veto legislation passed by the Democratic majorities. The four outstanding House races include contests in Minnesota and Tennessee and two Louisiana runoffs scheduled for December; the results could increase the Democrats’ majority [5][11].

If you don’t feel a sense of urgency and pressure in this job, and a desperation to deliver for folks, then you don’t belong under this Capitol dome.

— Rep. Jason Crow, Colorado Democrat (South China Morning Post)

Key Points

  • Narrow recount: Hubbard beat Foxx by 330 votes; North Carolina law allows a recount when the margin is below 1% [5][29].
  • Caucus differences: Rep. Troy Carter says Democrats are “not a monolith” and members bring different ideas [1].
  • Competitive districts: A Democratic campaign committee memo said the party won 70 of the 92 House districts it had identified as battlegrounds [31].
  • Senate leadership: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer [26].

Perspectives

White House: The administration warned that proposed Democratic investigations could amount to “blatant criminality” [15][14].

Sources: Financial Times

Sen. Mark Kelly: The Arizona Democrat says Congress should investigate the Iran war’s strategy and spending, asking who set the targets and why tens of billions of dollars in munitions were used [14].

Sources: Financial Times

President Donald Trump: After saying he would accept the election results and work with Democrats, Trump posted an image of a red cap marked “VETO” [12][24].

Sources: The Hindu

Rep. Jim Jordan: The Ohio Republican, selected to lead House Republicans in the minority, said the party would fight to regain power [11][16].

Sources: Euronews

Timeline

  • 3 November 2026: Voters cast ballots in midterm elections for Congress [12][26].
  • 20 November 2026: Trump issued an order seeking to limit information Congress can obtain [14].
  • 22 November 2026: Hubbard won the recount by 330 votes, flipping Foxx’s North Carolina seat [15][5].
  • 1 December 2026: Senate Democrats are scheduled to choose their party leader [26].
  • 3 January 2027: The new Congress convenes [11][1].

Historical Background

Foxx had represented North Carolina’s 5th Congressional District since 2005 and defeated Hubbard by nine percentage points in the 2024 midterms [5][29]. Hubbard’s recount victory flipped a district long held by Republicans [29].

Q&A

Q: What can the Democratic Senate do beyond passing legislation?

A: The Senate can confirm or block President Trump’s Cabinet and judicial nominees [5][29].

Gadi Eisenkot, the opposition leader tasked with forming Israel’s next government, called the attacks “Jewish terrorism” and urged arrests and severe sanctions. Indonesia confirms 24 dead as rescuers search candy factory ruins

Category: World

Indonesian authorities on Monday confirmed 24 deaths and said about 30 workers remained missing after a weekend fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, west of Jakarta [2][3][5]. Rescuers continued searching the burned site, where unstable structures and lingering hot spots endangered crews; 29 people were confirmed safe, including five who were hospitalized [2][3]. The factory’s chief executive, Steven Erwin Wijaya, said about 300 people were at the complex for Saturday’s shift [3][2]. Presidential labor adviser Said Iqbal said investigators were assessing whether safety protocols had been followed. He said preliminary information pointed to a possible air-conditioner short circuit, but authorities have not established the cause [3][2]. The fire left many remains too badly damaged for visual identification, so police are collecting DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings. Identification could take two to three weeks [5][2]. Search operations and the safety inquiry are continuing [3][2].

Ontario Liberal leader Bains to meet caucus Monday without legislative seat

Category: Canada

Ontario Liberal Leader Navdeep Bains is due to appear with his 14-member caucus at Queen’s Park on Monday, but he cannot challenge Premier Doug Ford in the legislature because he has no seat. Bains won the leadership of the third-place party on Saturday, narrowly defeating Toronto-area member of provincial parliament Lee Fairclough. He says he will seek elected office but has not identified a riding or timetable [1][5]. Bains said he would first consult party executives and caucus members. He ruled out asking a sitting Liberal member to resign to make way for a by-election. He inherits a party that has struggled to regain ground since losing power in 2018 and says it must build a team and platform before the next election, which could be held as late as 2030 [1][5][6].

  • Campaign finances: Ontario Liberal president Kathryn McGarry said the party had paid off its 2025 campaign debt, allowing donor contributions to be directed toward the next campaign [5].

item.content:encoded:
ESA reports software-related thruster glitch during BepiColombo's Mercury arrival

Category: Science

The European Space Agency (ESA) said a software issue shortened one of BepiColombo’s thruster burns during its Mercury orbit insertion. The joint European-Japanese spacecraft entered orbit successfully on Nov. 21 and remains safe. Mission teams at the European Space Operations Centre are investigating the cause, and ESA said it would provide an update on Monday, Nov. 23 [5][15][4]. BepiColombo carries two orbiters that have traveled together for eight years: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio. They are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with routine science operations planned to begin in April 2027 [5][2][4]. The mission will investigate Mercury’s interior, magnetic field and surface, including the origins of its polar ice and unusual surface hollows. ESA said teams were investigating the issue and would provide further information on Monday [5][4].

I think it's a little bit of an under-loved planet in the inner Solar System, but I think that's one of the reasons why it is so compelling

— Professor Emma Bunce, University of Leicester principal investigator on the mission (BBC News)

Key Points

  • Different orbits: After separation, ESA’s orbiter is scheduled to pass as close as 480 kilometers from Mercury, while Japan’s Mio will follow an elliptical path reaching about 11,000 kilometers away [20].
  • Instrument payload: The European orbiter carries spectrometers, a surface altimeter and gravity-measuring instruments; its radio-science experiment will help determine the size of Mercury’s core [6].
  • Swiss contribution: Neuchâtel company Micro-Cameras & Space Exploration built cameras to monitor spacecraft components and record flybys; University of Bern teams led development of the BELA laser altimeter and STROFIO mass spectrometer [19].
  • Thermal challenge: Mercury’s surface can exceed 400°C, so mission engineers must keep the spacecraft and instruments cool while they operate in intense solar radiation [1][11].
  • Surface terrain: Mercury has expanses of smooth terrain as well as cliffs reaching about 1.6 kilometers high [5].

Perspectives

Professor Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester principal investigator on the mission, said its scientific goals range from understanding how Mercury formed and evolved to studying its interaction with the Sun and extreme space weather [3].

Sources: BBC News

Geraint Jones, BepiColombo’s lead project scientist, highlighted the mission’s ability to compare simultaneous measurements from two spacecraft at Mercury, describing the data as unprecedented [1].

Sources: Associated Press, published by Phys.org

Timeline

  • 2018: BepiColombo launched from French Guiana aboard an Ariane 5 rocket [7]
  • 2024: A thruster-power problem forced a route adjustment and delayed arrival at Mercury [6]
  • 21 November 2026: A braking maneuver put the spacecraft into orbit around Mercury [5][4]
  • 22 November 2026: ESA disclosed that a software issue had shortened the orbit-insertion thruster burn [5][4]
  • 9 December 2026: The European and Japanese orbiters are scheduled to separate [5][2]

Scientific Significance

  • Planetary interior: Measurements from the orbiters’ instruments are intended to constrain the structure of Mercury’s unusually large iron core and test explanations for how the planet acquired it [7][6].
  • Core origin: Professor Emma Bunce said Mercury may have lost much of its mantle in a major collision or a series of impacts, though it may instead have formed in a metal-rich region of the early solar system [3].

Historical Background

NASA’s Mariner 10 made three flybys of Mercury in the 1970s, and NASA’s MESSENGER spacecraft became the first to orbit the planet in 2011 before its mission ended in 2015 [1][5]. BepiColombo is the first spacecraft to return to Mercury orbit since MESSENGER [7].

Q&A

Q: What work remains after the orbiters separate?

A: Mio is expected to settle into its final orbit, while the European orbiter must make additional engine burns before reaching its own target orbit around March 10, 2027 [4].

item.title: Deep-sea robot finds deepest volcanic deposits near Challenger Deep
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Science / Ocean Geology)
item.description: The remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea has found what researchers describe as the deepest documented underwater pyroclastic deposits, on the Mariana Trench wall about 6,000 meters below sea level [1][3][5]. The rocks provide evidence of volcanic flows in the trench’s western forearc, where geologists expected little volcanic activity because the mantle is generally not hot enough to melt [1][4]. The findings were published Nov. 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science [3][5]. The team’s observations support the idea that the Pacific Plate bends steeply as it sinks beneath the Mariana plate. That could help explain Challenger Deep’s depth and bring magma-generating processes closer to the trench [5][4]. But researchers have not identified the eruption sites or established how eruptions could produce these deposits under immense water pressure. They say further sampling and radiometric dating are needed. Jason/Medea cannot reach the seafloor below 6,500 meters, while Challenger Deep extends to about 11,000 meters [1][4].
item.content:encoded:
Deep-sea robot finds deepest volcanic deposits near Challenger Deep

Category: Science

The remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea has found what researchers describe as the deepest documented underwater pyroclastic deposits, on the Mariana Trench wall about 6,000 meters below sea level [1][3][5]. The rocks provide evidence of volcanic flows in the trench’s western forearc, where geologists expected little volcanic activity because the mantle is generally not hot enough to melt [1][4]. The findings were published Nov. 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science [3][5]. The team’s observations support the idea that the Pacific Plate bends steeply as it sinks beneath the Mariana plate. That could help explain Challenger Deep’s depth and bring magma-generating processes closer to the trench [5][4]. But researchers have not identified the eruption sites or established how eruptions could produce these deposits under immense water pressure. They say further sampling and radiometric dating are needed. Jason/Medea cannot reach the seafloor below 6,500 meters, while Challenger Deep extends to about 11,000 meters [1][4].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Imagining this happening is … pretty mind-boggling.

— William Chadwick, geologist at Oregon State University (Science News)

Key Points

  • Survey footprint: Jason/Medea made seven dives across roughly 300 kilometers of the forearc; researchers also examined the Shinaki Seep Field and retrieved fluid-sampling devices left by Japanese scientists in 2016 [1][2].
  • Unlocated source: The pyroclastic flows appear to have traveled only a short distance because they retained enough heat to fuse into hard rock. They would have lost that heat on a longer journey [1][4].

Perspectives

Sune Nielsen, a geochemist at the University of Lorraine, described the finding as perplexing and said there was no clear explanation [3].

Sources: Live Science

William Chadwick, a geologist at Oregon State University, said Challenger Deep may be uniquely suited to explosive volcanism in the super-deep ocean [5].

Sources: Science News

Technical Details

  • Supercritical fluid hypothesis: Researchers propose that water released from magma could enter a supercritical state under extreme pressure, potentially producing dense, fragmented deposits without the gas expansion typical of surface eruptions. This mechanism has not been confirmed [3][5].
  • Forearc extension: The study distinguishes mechanical plate stretching, inferred from older eastern rocks, from the addition of magma, suggested by younger western volcanic rocks. Additional sampling and radiometric dating are needed to establish the difference [1][4].

Scientific Significance

  • Distinctive trench segment: Unlike the better-known volcanic-arc pattern, the Challenger Deep segment has no organized volcanic arc; an ocean ridge lies there instead [3].
  • Potential regional effects: As the forearc stretches, the associated subduction zone may widen, which researchers say could affect plate motions in the western Pacific [1][4].

Historical Background

The Mariana Trench formed about 52 million years ago as the Pacific Plate began sliding beneath the Philippine Sea Plate [1][4].

item.content:encoded:
Army schedules 68-barrel Iowa blast despite court-ordered pause

Category: Science

The U.S. Army plans to detonate 68 barrels of degraded lead azide on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, despite a federal appeals court order pausing the explosives disposal permit. The Army says it will rely on a separate emergency exception to proceed, arguing that the material could explode without warning as temperatures fall [11][13]. The Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice challenged the plan over the risk that a blast could spread lead-bearing dust. The Justice Department says a controlled detonation is safer than an uncontrolled explosion. The groups say invoking emergency powers would bypass the court’s review and have asked to submit additional evidence challenging the Army’s risk assessment [3][17][13]. The Army moved the operation from Monday to Wednesday, saying the later date allows for favorable weather and time to put mitigation measures in place [18][11]. The groups’ legal challenge remains active, while the Army says it intends to proceed under the emergency exception [13][9].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Anyone can claim an emergency at any point and do whatever they want. I don’t think people can or should accept that.

— Thien Chau, Earthjustice attorney (Al Jazeera)

Key Points

  • Alternative disposal: The Army hired a contractor to turn the explosives into harmless waste but later abandoned that approach in favor of detonating them in place [5].
  • Range estimates: Army projections have varied. Iowa officials’ reporting cited a recent model showing lead dust settling across an area about 25 miles long and 5 miles wide, while earlier plume estimates extended as far as 100 miles, depending on weather [18][3].
  • Blast-control concerns: Environmental engineer Ranajit Sahu questioned whether the proposed controls would adequately protect public health [9].
  • Farm concerns: Iowa agriculture officials advised nearby cattle farmers to move livestock, feed and equipment indoors or elsewhere, but farmers told the Iowa Environmental Council that keeping cattle indoors was not viable [11].
  • Local response: Mediapolis announced a school cancellation and library closure, and its school district said it would buy lead test kits to sample school grounds and buildings [4].

Perspectives

U.S. Army: The Army says the doors to the explosives’ storage bunker were removed in preparation for the planned blast and cannot be reinstalled, leaving the material more exposed to temperature changes [8].

Sources: WGN Radio

Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice: The groups say the Army’s storage and inspection practices allowed the lead azide to deteriorate, describing the emergency as one of the Army’s own making [9].

Sources: KOAT

Mark J. Thomas, former Environmental Protection Agency air-monitoring official: Thomas disputed the Army’s claim that cooling would make delay unsafe, saying the semi-underground structure would shield the drums from the full temperature change [9].

Sources: KOAT

Iowa Senator-elect Josh Turek: Turek called for a full investigation into why the stockpile was allowed to degrade, whether other dangerous materials are stored at the plant and how future failures can be prevented [13].

Sources: CBS News

Timeline

  • March 2026: Army monitoring found recrystallized lead azide in storage bunkers [19]
  • 15 October 2026: Army officials held a community meeting about possible detonation plans [19]
  • 13 November 2026: EPA approved an emergency permit for controlled detonation [19]
  • 20 November 2026: Originally scheduled blast was postponed after public and official objections [19]
  • 20 November 2026: Federal appeals court paused the plan after environmental groups sued [3]
  • 22 November 2026: Army announced a Wednesday detonation, citing weather and mitigation preparations [11]

Technical Details

  • Recrystallization: As liquid in the drums evaporated, needle-shaped lead azide crystals formed. The Army says the crystals are sensitive to friction and impact, making the barrels unsafe to open or move [3][8].
  • Blast controls: The Army’s plan uses earth-covered concrete magazines and sand barriers, with soil saturated and water sprayed before and during detonation to limit dust dispersal [7].

Scientific Significance

  • Lead exposure: Lead can damage the brain and nervous system, particularly in children. The environmental groups are concerned that deposited particles could reach homes, farmland and waterways [11][18].
  • Exposure measurement: University of Iowa professor David Cwiertny said field sampling after the blast would be needed to determine where lead settles, since farm fields and topsoil cannot simply be wiped clean like household surfaces [3].
  • Uncertainty in plume models: The Army’s maps depend on real-time wind conditions, and reported projections differ in the area they predict will be affected. Air and surface sampling after the blast would measure actual exposure [3][18].

Humanitarian Impact

The blast could produce loud noise and ground vibrations, with officials warning that windows could break; residents near Middletown City Park and Butterfly Park were told to leave for six hours to avoid vibration risks [18][3].

Q&A

Q: Will Illinois also monitor for effects from the plume?

A: The Illinois Environmental Protection Agency said it would watch data from its northern Illinois air-monitoring network for signs of impacts on Illinois communities [7].

Action Items

  • Follow local shelter and evacuation instructions if you are in the affected area: The Army advises people who cannot leave to remain indoors, close windows and doors, and turn off heating or cooling systems that bring in outside air during the exposure period [7].
  • Protect outdoor items and children’s play surfaces after officials end the exposure period: The Army advises wet-cleaning surfaces children may touch. Residents should follow local and Army guidance on when cleanup can begin [7].

November Beaver Moon begins series of close full moons through February

Category: Science

November’s full Beaver Moon peaks at 9:53 a.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, Nov. 24, when it will be below the horizon in North America. Observers there can look for it rising around sunset. The moon will be about 224,170 miles from Earth, close enough to qualify as a supermoon under some definitions, and should appear only slightly larger and brighter than an average full moon [2][1][3]. The next full moon falls on Dec. 24 and is expected to be the closest in the sequence, at about 221,667 miles. Further full moons are due Jan. 22 and Feb. 20. Sources describe the sequence as either three or four consecutive supermoons [2][1]. Near moonrise, the moon may look especially large because of the horizon-related “moon illusion,” not because it is closer at that moment [3][1].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Key Points

  • Pleiades pairing: On Nov. 24, the moon will pass about 0.9 degrees from the Pleiades star cluster, though its brightness may obscure the cluster’s fainter stars [3].
  • Best viewing: The moon will appear full to the naked eye on Monday and Wednesday as well as Tuesday [2][7].
  • Coastal tides: People’s Daily Digital reported coastal preparations with sandbags, berms and pumps in Laguna Beach and other shoreline areas ahead of possible high-tide flooding [5].
  • Other planets: On the night of Nov. 24-25, Mars and Jupiter are expected to be visible in the eastern sky, Saturn in the southwest, and Venus before dawn [6].

Timeline

  • 24 December 2026: Cold Moon expected to pass about 221,667 miles from Earth [2][9]
  • 22 January 2027: Wolf Moon expected as another close full Moon [2][1]
  • 20 February 2027: Snow Moon forecast to complete the four-month sequence [1][7]

Action Items

  • Look for the moon’s orange tint shortly after moonrise. Near the horizon, its light travels through more of the atmosphere, where blue wavelengths are scattered more strongly [9].
